mainTopic: Collecting a כתובה with only a גט or only a כתובה document, whether a שובר is written, and רב's rule splitting the עיקר and the תוספת
overview: The amud opens at the end of a משנה case: a woman who shows her גט but not her כתובה document still collects her כתובה. In the reverse case, she has a כתובה but no גט, and she cannot collect. A creditor with no פרוזבול after שביעית is treated the same way. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that in the time of persecution both collect without the missing document. The גמרא learns from the first case that a שובר (receipt) is written when a debt is paid. רב rejects this proof by setting the משנה in a place where no כתובה is written. שמואל, as explained by רב ענן, makes it a question of who must bring proof. רב then changes his mind: a גט collects the עיקר and a כתובה collects the תוספת. The גמרא challenges רב, asking why the woman with a כתובה does not at least collect the תוספת. רב יוסף begins to answer with a case where there are no witnesses to the divorce, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: With a divorce document alone, she collects
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of the previous משנה case: a woman who shows her גט, even without the כתובה document, collects her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: She collects her marriage contract payment.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a ruling in the משנה that started before this section. A woman who has her גט but not her כתובה document still collects her כתובה money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every Jewish woman is owed a כתובה, so the גט by itself proves she is divorced and owed money. The husband cannot claim he already paid her unless he has proof. The גמרא will soon use exactly this ruling to learn something new.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract, and the money it promises the wife at divorce or widowhood

phrases.english: She collects her marriage contract payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה case that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman with a גט but no כתובה document collects her כתובה.

steps.title: Marriage contract without a divorce document, and a loan without a prosbol
steps.stepSummary: If she shows a כתובה but no גט and says the גט was lost, while he says his שובר was lost, she does not collect. The same applies to a creditor who has no פרוזבול after שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she shows a marriage contract but no divorce document, and she says, 'My divorce document was lost,' and he says, 'My receipt was lost,' and likewise a creditor who shows a loan document without a prosbol, these are not paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reverse case. Without a גט, the woman cannot collect even though she has the כתובה document, and a creditor without a פרוזבול cannot collect after שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband answers her claim with the same kind of claim: if she can say her גט got lost, he can say his receipt got lost. Without a גט nothing proves she is owed anything now. The creditor is the same: without a פרוזבול, שביעית cancels the loan, and he cannot simply say he once had one.

keyTerms.meaning: A receipt showing a debt was paid
A document that keeps שביעית from cancelling a loan

phrases.english: A marriage contract, and there is no divorce document with it,
she says: My divorce document was lost.
And he says: My receipt was lost.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן בַּעַל חוֹב שֶׁהוֹצִיא שְׁטַר חוֹב
phrases.english: And likewise, a creditor who brought out a loan document
and there is no prosbol with it,
phrases.notes: This is after שביעית, when a loan without a פרוזבול is cancelled.

phrases.english: these are not paid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to step 1: a כתובה without a גט instead of a גט without a כתובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כתובה without a גט, or a loan document without a פרוזבול after שביעית, cannot be collected.

steps.title: In times of danger, no divorce document or prosbol is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that from the time of persecution onward, a woman collects without a גט and a creditor collects without a פרוזבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: From the time of danger onward, a woman collects her marriage contract without a divorce document, and a creditor collects without a prosbol.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the previous ruling for a specific period, the time of danger. Then, a missing גט or פרוזבול does not stop collection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the persecution, keeping these religious documents was dangerous, so people destroyed them right after they were written. Because of that, a missing document no longer suggests anything suspicious, and the court assumes it really existed.

keyTerms.meaning: Danger; here, the period of persecution by the rulers

steps.whatToRemember: Normal rule: no גט means no כתובה payment, and no פרוזבול means no loan payment after שביעית. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: in times of danger, both are collected without the document.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
From the time of danger and onward,
phrases.notes: This means the time when the rulers banned מצוות, so people did not keep these documents.

phrases.english: a woman collects her marriage contract without a divorce document,
and a creditor collects without a prosbol.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: מִן הַסַּכָּנָה וְאֵילָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a time-based exception to the ruling in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the time of danger onward, a כתובה is collected without a גט and a loan without a פרוזבול.

steps.title: Learning from the first case that a receipt is written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from the case of a גט without a כתובה that courts write a שובר when a debt is paid. Otherwise we would worry she could collect a second time with the כתובה document.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Learn from this that a receipt is written. Because if a receipt were not written, we should worry that she might later bring out her marriage contract and collect with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and draws a conclusion from the משנה's first case (step 1): when a debt is paid, a שובר is written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 1 she collects with only her גט, while the כתובה document is still somewhere out there. If no שובר were written, she could later show that כתובה in another court and get paid again, and the משנה would not have let her collect. Since the משנה does let her collect, the husband must get a שובר to protect himself.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This proof comes from the first case (a גט without a כתובה, step 1), not from the case of the lost receipt in step 2.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether a שובר is written, or the lender must instead return the loan document, is a basic question for paying back any debt.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Learn from this that a receipt is written.
phrases.notes: This is learned from the first case, where she collects with only her גט.

phrases.english: For if a receipt were not written,
let us worry that she might bring out her marriage contract,
and collect with it.
phrases.notes: He means a second time, perhaps in a different court, since the husband would have no proof he paid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's first ruling (step 1) and draws a new rule from it.
steps.raayaObject: That when a debt is paid, a שובר is written.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that a woman with a גט but no כתובה document collects. This only makes sense if a שובר protects the husband from a second collection.

steps.title: רב: The משנה is about a place with no written כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב rejects the proof that courts write a שובר. He says the משנה is talking about a place where no כתובה document is written at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: We are dealing with a place where people do not write a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב pushes back on the proof from step 4. He says the משנה's case does not show that courts write a שובר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof worked like this: she collects with only a גט, so we must not be worried that she will later bring the כתובה document and collect again. That only makes sense if a שובר is written. רב answers that in her town no כתובה document exists at all, so there is nothing she could bring later and no need for a שובר.

keyTerms.meaning: A receipt showing a debt was paid

phrases.english: Rav said:
We are dealing with a place where they do not write a marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין כּוֹתְבִין כְּתוּבָּה עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 4 by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that courts write a שובר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed she has a כתובה document that she could bring later. In a place where none is written, there is nothing to fear and no need for a שובר.

steps.title: שמואל: Even where they write a כתובה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the משנה applies even in a place where a כתובה document is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Even in a place where they write a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב. He says the משנה's rule (she collects with just a גט) holds even where a כתובה document is normally written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In such a place she probably has a כתובה document, so it seems we would worry she could collect twice. That makes it sound like שמואל agrees courts write a שובר. The גמרא will question this right away.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Even in a place where they write a marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אַף בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁכּוֹתְבִין כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רב's narrowing in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's rule applies even in a place where a כתובה is written.

steps.title: Does שמואל hold that courts write a receipt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, according to שמואל, courts really write a שובר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to שמואל, do we write a שובר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about שמואל's view. It sets up רב ענן's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she collects with a גט even in a place where כתובה documents are written, the only way to stop her from collecting twice seems to be a שובר. The גמרא asks whether שמואל really means that.

phrases.english: And according to Shmuel, does one write a receipt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what follows from שמואל's view in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does שמואל's view mean that courts write a שובר?

steps.title: רב ענן explains שמואל: Whoever claims the unusual must prove it
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן heard directly from שמואל how to read the משנה. Where no כתובה is written and the husband says he wrote one, he must prove it. Where a כתובה is written and she says he did not write her one, she must prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said: It was explained to me by שמואל himself. In a place where they do not write a כתובה, if he says 'I wrote one,' he must bring proof. In a place where they do write one, if she says 'He did not write me one,' she must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן answers the question. שמואל was not talking about a שובר. He was talking about who has to bring proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a place where they write a כתובה, she collects with only a גט if she proves no כתובה was ever written. Then there is no document she could use to collect again, so no שובר is needed. The person whose claim goes against the local custom is the one who must prove it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל (as explained by רב ענן), the משנה does not prove that courts write a שובר. She collects with a גט in a place where כתובות are written only if she proves none was written for her.

phrases.english: Rav Anan said:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: It was explained to me by Master Shmuel himself:
In a place where they do not write, and he said, 'I wrote one'
he must bring proof.
In a place where they write, and she said, 'He did not write me one'
she must bring proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עָנָן: לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל does not need a שובר. In a place where they write a כתובה, she collects with a גט only after proving none was written, so she cannot collect twice.

steps.title: רב changes his mind: With a גט she collects the base amount, with a כתובה only the extra
steps.stepSummary: רב retracted his earlier reading. In any place, with a גט she collects the basic amount (עיקר), and with a כתובה document she collects only the added amount (תוספת). Anyone who wants to object is welcome to try.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even רב changed his mind, for רב said: Whether in a place where they write a כתובה or in a place where they don't, with a גט she collects the base amount, and with a כתובה she collects the extra amount. Whoever wants to answer back, let him come and answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רב took back his view from step 5. He gives a new rule that works in every place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger was that she could collect twice: once with the גט and once with the כתובה. רב solves this by splitting the payment. The גט gets her only the עיקר, the minimum the rabbis set. The כתובה document gets her only the תוספת, the extra her husband added. So even in two different courts she can never get more than she is owed, and no שובר is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The base amount of the כתובה set by the rabbis
The extra amount the husband added

steps.whatToRemember: רב's final view: a גט collects the עיקר and a כתובה collects the תוספת, so double collection is impossible in any place.
steps.confusionAlert: רב does mean that a woman who brings only her כתובה document does not collect the עיקר. The husband can say she already collected it with her גט. Step 11 builds on exactly this: 'fine, she does not collect the basic amount.'

phrases.english: And even Rav retracted,
for Rav said:
Whether in a place where they write,
or in a place where they do not write,
with a bill of divorce, she collects the base amount.
phrases.notes: The base amount is 200 זוז for a בתולה and 100 for a widow or divorcee.

phrases.english: With a marriage contract, she collects the additional amount.
And whoever wishes to object, let him come and object.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַב הֲדַר בֵּיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports that רב dropped his reading from step 5 and gives his new rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule protects the husband from paying twice without needing any שובר, and it works the same everywhere.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In every place, a גט collects the עיקר and a כתובה collects the תוספת.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: a כתובה without a גט is not paid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if she has a כתובה but no גט, she says the גט was lost and he says the שובר was lost, she does not collect. The same is true for a creditor with no פרוזבול. This sets up a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: She brings a כתובה with no גט. She says 'My גט was lost,' and he says 'My שובר was lost.' And likewise a creditor who brings a loan document with no פרוזבול. These are not paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה again, this time to start a challenge. This step sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that a woman holding a כתובה without a גט gets nothing at all. רב just said that a כתובה document collects the תוספת. The next step spells out the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A document that keeps a loan collectable after שביעית

phrases.english: We learned:
A marriage contract with no bill of divorce with it,
she says, 'My bill of divorce was lost,'
and he says, 'My receipt was lost.'

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן בַּעַל חוֹב שֶׁהוֹצִיא שְׁטַר חוֹב
phrases.english: And likewise a creditor who brought out a loan document
and has no prosbol with it,
phrases.notes: This is after שביעית, when loans without a פרוזבול are cancelled.

phrases.english: these are not paid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the משנה from step 2 to begin a challenge after רב's new rule in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule in step 9 that a כתובה document collects the תוספת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says a woman holding only a כתובה collects nothing at all. According to רב, a כתובה document collects the תוספת, so she should get at least that. The full challenge is spelled out in the next step.

steps.title: The משנה fits שמואל but seems to clash with רב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה works well for שמואל. For רב, though, the woman holding a כתובה should at least collect the תוספת.
steps.simpleTranslation: For שמואל this is fine. He reads the משנה as a place where people don't write a כתובה, and the husband says 'I wrote one.' We tell him: bring proof. If he has no proof, we tell him: go pay her. But for רב: fine, she can't collect the basic amount, but she should at least collect the added amount!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the משנה from step 10 fits שמואל's approach easily. It then asks why the same משנה doesn't contradict רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said in step 9 that a כתובה document is what collects the תוספת, since a גט alone only collects the עיקר. So when she shows a כתובה, the husband can claim he already paid the עיקר through her גט, but he cannot claim he paid the תוספת that way. Why, then, does the משנה say she collects nothing at all?

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this works fine for (one opinion)
But (for the other opinion, there is a problem)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether she collects the full amount. The גמרא agrees she can't collect the עיקר. It only asks why she loses the תוספת too.

phrases.english: Granted, according to שמואל,
he sets it in a place where they do not write a כתובה,
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה. This is the reading רב ענן reported in step 8.

phrases.english: and the husband said: I wrote one,
where we say to him: bring proof,
and if he does not bring proof,
we say to him: go pay her.
But according to רב:
fine, she does not collect the basic amount,
but she should at least collect the added amount!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge set up in step 10 by showing the משנה fits שמואל but not רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view (step 9) that a כתובה document collects the תוספת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט alone could never have collected the תוספת. So the husband's claim that he paid through the גט cannot cover it, and she should collect the תוספת. Yet the משנה says she collects nothing.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The case has no witnesses to the divorce
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף sets the משנה in a case with no divorce witnesses. That gives the husband a מיגו: he could have said he never divorced her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What case are we dealing with here? One where there are no witnesses to the divorce. Since the husband could have said 'I never divorced her'...
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף begins defending רב by narrowing the משנה to a specific case. His sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no one saw the divorce, the husband could have denied divorcing her at all, and then she would get nothing. Because he could have made that stronger claim, the גמרא is building toward believing his weaker claim that he paid her. That would explain why she loses even the תוספת.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a source to a specific case)
Since he could have made a stronger claim, we believe the claim he did make

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף's sentence is not finished here. The 'since he could say' sets up a conclusion that comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
What case are we dealing with here?
Where there are no witnesses to the divorce there.
Since he could say: I did not divorce her,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by limiting the משנה to a case with no divorce witnesses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to apply to every case, so she should collect the תוספת according to רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה applies when there are no divorce witnesses. The husband then has a מיגו that supports his claim. The answer is completed on the next amud.
